The committee's report was so ___ that even its critics praised its clarity.
'Lucid' means clear and easy to understand, which explains why even critics praised the report.
Despite repeated warnings, the contractor remained ___ and continued to ignore safety norms.
'Obdurate' means stubbornly refusing to change one's attitude or course of action.
The new policy is expected to ___ the burden on small taxpayers.
'Alleviate' means to make a burden or difficulty less severe.
Her ___ remarks during the debate won her the respect of both sides.
'Astute' means perceptive and clever, which is why the remarks earned respect.
The village was ___ by the floods, and relief teams could not reach it for three days.
'Marooned' means trapped and unable to leave, as the village was by floodwater.
He was ___ for his careless remarks about the community.
'Castigated' means severely criticised, which fits the reaction to careless remarks.
The two countries agreed to ___ their differences and work towards peace.
'Bury their differences' is the fixed expression meaning to stop quarrelling and reconcile.
The scientist's theory was initially ___, but later experiments confirmed it.
'Ridiculed' contrasts correctly with the later confirmation of the theory.
A ___ of bees settled on the branch, forcing the children to retreat.
The standard collective noun for bees is a 'swarm'.
The manager asked for a ___ account of the incident, without any exaggeration.
'Factual' means based on facts, which matches the phrase 'without any exaggeration'.
She is not only a talented singer ___ an accomplished dancer.
The correlative conjunction 'not only ... but also' must be used in pairs.
The teacher, along with her students, ___ attending the seminar.
With 'along with', the verb agrees with the first subject 'the teacher', which is singular.
He has been living in Delhi ___ 2015.
'Since' is used with a point of time such as a year, while 'for' is used with a duration.
Hardly had the bell rung ___ the students rushed out of the class.
'Hardly had ... when' is the correct correlative structure; 'than' goes with 'no sooner'.
No sooner had he arrived ___ the meeting began.
'No sooner ... than' is the fixed pair; 'when' would be used with 'hardly' or 'scarcely'.
She is one of the few candidates who ___ the eligibility test.
In 'one of the few candidates who ...', 'who' refers to the plural 'candidates', so a plural verb is required.
The report, ___ was submitted yesterday, contains several errors.
'Which' is the relative pronoun used for things such as a report.
He is the only person ___ I can trust completely.
The relative pronoun is the object of 'trust', so the objective form 'whom' is required.
Scarcely had we started ___ it began to rain heavily.
'Scarcely had ... when' is the correct fixed structure.
Neither the manager nor the employees ___ willing to accept the new terms.
With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'employees', which is plural.
The proposal was ___ by the board, ___ the objections raised by the finance team.
'Despite' introduces the objections as a contrast to the board's approval.
___ the heavy traffic, we ___ the airport on time.
'Despite' is followed by a noun phrase, and 'reached' fits the positive result of arriving on time.
The teacher spoke ___ so that even the weakest students could ___ her.
Speaking slowly helps weaker students follow the explanation.
The company's profits ___ sharply last year, ___ the management to revise its expansion plans.
A sharp fall in profits would force management to revise its expansion plans.
___ he was ill, he ___ to attend the meeting.
'Although' introduces a concessive clause, and 'managed' shows he attended despite the illness.
The new bridge is not only ___ but also ___, saving both time and money.
Both adjectives must be positive to match the idea of saving time and money.
She was ___ tired ___ she fell asleep immediately.
'So + adjective + that' expresses the result of being extremely tired.
The judge asked the witness to ___ his statement ___ any exaggeration.
A witness is asked to repeat a statement 'without' exaggeration, so 'reiterate' and 'without' fit.
___ the storm, the flight was delayed, ___ the passengers had to wait for hours.
'Owing to' introduces the cause, and 'and' joins the two resulting facts.
The candidate's answers were ___ but ___, impressing the interviewers with both depth and clarity.
The praise for 'depth and clarity' requires both adjectives to be positive.
The manager's decision to promote the junior over the senior employee ___.
'Raised many eyebrows' means caused surprise or disapproval, which fits an unexpected promotion.
When the auditor began asking about the missing files, the accountant realised that ___.
A) he had bitten the bullet
B) the ball was in his court
C) the writing was on the wall
D) he had kept the ball rolling
E) he had buried the hatchet
'The writing is on the wall' means clear signs of trouble ahead, which matches the auditor's questioning.
The government's new credit scheme is a ___ in the arm for small businesses.
'A shot in the arm' is the fixed idiom meaning an encouraging boost.
He is so ___ that he never admits his mistakes.
'Obstinate' means stubbornly refusing to change, which explains never admitting mistakes.
The two brothers decided to ___ the hatchet after years of estrangement.
'Bury the hatchet' is the idiom meaning to end a quarrel and make peace.
Her explanation was so ___ that no one could find fault with it.
'Cogent' means clear, logical and convincing, so no fault could be found.
The project was ___ because of insufficient funding.
'Shelved' means postponed or set aside, which follows from a lack of funds.
The teacher's praise acted as a ___ for the shy student to speak up.
A 'catalyst' triggers change; praise encouraged the student to speak.
The witness's statement was ___ with the evidence, strengthening the prosecution's case.
'Consistent with' means in agreement with, which strengthens a case.
It is ___ that the meeting be postponed until the chairman returns.
'It is essential that ... be ...' uses the subjunctive and expresses necessity.
